sec('Section 13 - Intellectual Property and Confidentiality',
 'Despite its heading, Section 13 contains no assignment of intellectual property. The confidentiality carve-outs are also overbroad, in particular the carve-out for "general knowledge, skills, and experience ... acquired during ... employment." The DTSA notice is compliant.',
 [
 dict(id='58', sec='13(a) (Carve-Out)', title='Overbroad confidentiality carve-outs: prior knowledge and unqualified "general knowledge, skills and experience" acquired at Pinnacle',
  sev='High', cat=MR, impact='Could permit use of formulations, manufacturing processes and pricing learned at Pinnacle',
  draft='Excludes information (ii) known to the Executive before disclosure, as shown by her records, (iii) received from a third party not "to the Executive\'s knowledge" bound by confidentiality, and (iv) her "general knowledge, skills, and experience, including ... acquired during the course of the Executive\'s employment with the Company."',
  base='Playbook Section IX.A permits only: public information, information from third parties not under confidentiality obligations, legally compelled disclosure (with notice) and DTSA disclosures. A general-skills carve-out must be narrowly drafted using the standard language. Term Sheet Section 14: confidentiality survives in perpetuity.',
  analysis=['Carve-out (iv) is the most dangerous. For an executive with a Ph.D. in chemical engineering who will oversee product formulation and manufacturing, almost any process know-how could be described as "general knowledge ... acquired during employment." Carve-out (ii) would also cover information she brings from Meridian, which conflicts with the Section 1.6 representations.'],
  redline=['Carve-Out. Notwithstanding the foregoing, "Confidential Information" shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault, act, or omission of the Executive{+ and other than as a result of a breach of the Executive\'s obligations hereunder+}; {+or+} [-(ii) was lawfully known to the Executive prior to its disclosure by the Company, as evidenced by the Executive\'s contemporaneous written records; (iii)-]{+(ii)+} is lawfully received by the Executive from a third party who is not[-, to the Executive\'s knowledge,-] subject to any obligation of confidentiality with respect to such information[-; or (iv) constitutes the Executive\'s general knowledge, skills, and experience, including knowledge, skills, and experience acquired during the course of the Executive\'s employment with the Company-]. {+Nothing herein shall prevent the Executive from using general professional knowledge, skills, and experience that do not constitute Confidential Information as defined herein.+}'],
  comment='Conformed the carve-outs to the Company\'s standard confidentiality provisions. The Executive\'s general professional skills remain unrestricted to the extent they do not involve Confidential Information.'),
 dict(id='59', sec='13 (new 13(d))', title='No inventions/work-product assignment clause',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Company ownership of formulations, process improvements and other IP developed by the COO depends on default rules (work for hire and the hired-to-invent or shop-right doctrines), which give incomplete protection, especially for patentable inventions',
  draft='None, despite the section heading.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 14: customary inventions assignment consistent with the Company\'s standard IP Assignment Agreement for senior executives. Playbook Section IX.B: mandatory, "critical gap" if omitted. It covers inventions relating to the business, made with Company resources, or resulting from duties, with a carve-out for own-time inventions.',
  analysis=['Copyright work-for-hire rules do not cover patentable inventions. Without a present assignment ("hereby assigns"), the Company would be left with an implied-assignment or shop-right argument. North Carolina\'s statute, N.C. Gen. Stat. Section 66-57.1, makes unenforceable any assignment of inventions developed entirely on the employee\'s own time without Company resources that do not relate to the business or result from her work. Our carve-out tracks it.'],
  redline=['{+Section 13(d) - Inventions and Work Product. (i) The Executive hereby assigns, and agrees to assign, to the Company all right, title and interest in and to all inventions, discoveries, improvements, formulations, processes, innovations, works of authorship, designs, trade secrets and other intellectual property ("Inventions") conceived, developed, created or reduced to practice by the Executive, alone or jointly, during her employment that (A) relate to the actual or demonstrably anticipated business, research or development of the Company or any of its subsidiaries, (B) are developed using the Company\'s equipment, supplies, facilities, resources or Confidential Information, or (C) result from work performed by the Executive for the Company. All copyrightable Inventions shall be "works made for hire" to the extent permitted by law. (ii) This Section 13(d) does not apply to any Invention that the Executive developed entirely on her own time without using the Company\'s equipment, supplies, facilities, resources or Confidential Information and that neither relates to the Company\'s business or actual or demonstrably anticipated research or development nor results from work performed by the Executive for the Company, consistent with N.C. Gen. Stat. Section 66-57.1. (iii) The Executive shall promptly disclose all Inventions to the Company and, during and after her employment, execute all documents and take all actions reasonably requested to perfect, register and enforce the Company\'s rights, at the Company\'s expense, and hereby irrevocably appoints the Company as her attorney-in-fact for such purpose. (iv) Concurrently with this Agreement, the Executive shall execute the Company\'s standard Intellectual Property Assignment Agreement for senior executives, which shall be read together with this Section 13(d).+}'],
  comment='Added the Company\'s standard inventions and work-product assignment, including the statutory carve-out for inventions developed entirely on the Executive\'s own time.'),
 dict(id='60', sec='13 (new 13(e))', title='No protected-activity (whistleblower) carve-out',
  sev='Medium', cat=MR, impact='Regulatory exposure: SEC Rule 21F-17 enforcement actions have targeted confidentiality and release language that impedes reporting',
  draft='The DTSA notice is present (and compliant), but there is no general carve-out for communications with government agencies.',
  base='Playbook Section IX.A requires the DTSA notice. The protected-activity carve-out is recommended as a compliance matter (not addressed in the term sheet).',
  analysis=['The SEC has repeatedly brought Rule 21F-17 actions against issuers whose employment agreements or releases could be read to restrict reporting. The carve-out protects the Company and the enforceability of Section 13, and it costs nothing.'],
  redline=['{+Section 13(e) - Protected Activity. Nothing in this Agreement or in any other agreement or Company policy prohibits or restricts the Executive from filing a charge or complaint with, communicating with, providing information to, or participating in any investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission or any other federal, state or local governmental agency, or from receiving an award for information provided to any governmental agency, in each case without notice to the Company.+}'],
  comment='Added a customary protected-activity provision consistent with SEC rules.'),
 ])

sec('Section 15 - Dispute Resolution',
 'The draft puts all disputes in Minnesota courts, under Minnesota law, with one-way fee shifting in the Executive\'s favor. The term sheet requires AAA arbitration in Charlotte under North Carolina law, with each party bearing its own fees. The Minnesota choice of law is not just a home-court advantage: under Minn. Stat. Section 181.988 it would likely void the Company\'s non-compete outright.',
 [
 dict(id='61', sec='15.1', title='Exclusive forum: state/federal courts in Hennepin County, Minnesota (no arbitration)',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Litigation in the Executive\'s home forum, a jury, public filings. Defense costs higher than in arbitration',
  draft='Exclusive jurisdiction of Hennepin County, Minnesota courts for all claims.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 13: binding AAA arbitration under the Employment Rules, seated in Charlotte, Mecklenburg County. Playbook Section XV: single arbitrator, delegation of arbitrability, court carve-out for injunctive relief, class and collective action waiver, and jury waiver. Litigation elsewhere "must be rejected."',
  analysis=['The Executive will live and work in Charlotte. Hennepin County has no connection to the employment relationship other than her current residence. Note for the arbitration clause: the Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act of 2021 (9 U.S.C. Sections 401-402) lets her elect court for sexual harassment and assault claims, so the clause should acknowledge that.'],
  redline=['Section 15.1 - [-Exclusive Forum. Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement ... shall be resolved exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Hennepin County, Minnesota. Each Party hereby irrevocably consents to the personal jurisdiction and venue of such courts ...-]{+Arbitration. Except as provided in Section 12(f) and this Section 15.1, any dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the Executive\'s employment or the termination thereof, including the breach, termination, enforcement, interpretation or validity of this Agreement and the determination of the scope or applicability of this agreement to arbitrate, shall be resolved by final and binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association ("AAA") under its Employment Arbitration Rules and Mediation Procedures then in effect, before a single arbitrator experienced in executive employment matters. The seat of arbitration shall be Charlotte, Mecklenburg County, North Carolina. Either Party may seek temporary, preliminary or emergency injunctive relief in the state or federal courts located in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, to enforce Sections 12 or 13 without waiving the right to arbitrate. To the fullest extent permitted by law, the Parties waive any right to a jury trial and agree that claims may be brought only in an individual capacity and not as a plaintiff or class member in any class, collective or representative proceeding. This Section 15.1 shall not require arbitration of any claim that, under applicable law (including 9 U.S.C. Sections 401-402), may not be the subject of a mandatory pre-dispute arbitration agreement, at the Executive\'s election.+}'],
  comment='Disputes will be resolved by AAA arbitration in Charlotte, where the Executive will be employed, with a court carve-out for injunctive relief and the statutory exception for claims that cannot be subject to mandatory arbitration.'),
 dict(id='62', sec='15.2', title='Minnesota governing law (would likely void the Company\'s non-compete under Minn. Stat. Section 181.988)',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Would likely void Section 12(a) entirely and impose Minnesota employment-law rules on a North Carolina employment relationship',
  draft='Minnesota law governs, excluding conflict-of-laws rules.',
  base='Term Sheet Sections 10.D and 13: North Carolina law governs the agreement and the restrictive covenants. Playbook Section XV: NC law, which is "essential" for covenant enforcement.',
  analysis=['Minn. Stat. Section 181.988, subd. 2, makes covenants not to compete in agreements entered into on or after July 1, 2023 void and unenforceable (with narrow sale-of-business and dissolution exceptions). With Minnesota law governing, the Section 12(a) non-compete would almost certainly fail. A non-compete with a 6-month period and one product category may have been drafted with that outcome in mind.',
           'Related point: subd. 3 of the statute bars requiring an employee who "primarily resides and works in Minnesota" to accept a non-Minnesota choice of law or forum. Once she relocates and works in Charlotte, that provision should not apply. Two steps help foreclose the argument: (a) confirm her relocation timing, including whether her family stays in Minneapolis through the school year, and (b) recite in the agreement that her principal place of employment is Charlotte from the Effective Date. Corporate-law matters (indemnification, fiduciary duties) remain governed by Delaware law.'],
  redline=['Section 15.2 - Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of [-Minnesota-]{+North Carolina+}, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflict of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction{+; provided that matters relating to indemnification and the internal affairs of the Company shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware+}. All questions concerning the construction, validity, enforcement, and interpretation of this Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of [-Minnesota-]{+North Carolina+}, without regard to the conflicts of law principles thereof. {+The Parties acknowledge that the Executive\'s principal place of employment from and after the Effective Date shall be the Company\'s principal offices in Charlotte, North Carolina.+}'],
  comment='North Carolina law governs, since the Executive will live and work in North Carolina and the Company is headquartered there. Delaware law applies to corporate governance matters.'),
 dict(id='63', sec='15.3', title='One-sided fee shifting: Company pays Executive\'s fees if she prevails on "any material claim"',
  sev='High', cat=MR, impact='Uncapped. Funds litigation against the Company. Partial success on one claim shifts all of her fees',
  draft='The Company reimburses all of the Executive\'s fees if she prevails on any material claim. If the Company wins, each side bears its own fees.',

  redline=['Section 15.3 - Attorneys\' Fees. [-In the event of any dispute, controversy, litigation, or legal proceeding between the Parties ..., if the Executive prevails on any material claim asserted by or against the Executive in such proceeding, the Company shall reimburse the Executive for all reasonable attorneys\' fees, costs, disbursements, and expenses incurred by the Executive in connection with such dispute ... sec('New Provisions to Insert (Mandatory Omissions)',
